facts.raw_span: An 8-year-old girl was evaluated for recurrent seizures
left-sided weakness
developmental delays
Seizures began at age 3 months
no family history of neurological disorders
significant cognitive impairment
marked left hemiparesis with brisk reflexes
Electroencephalography showed focal abnormal brain activity
Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres
significant atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere
areas of cystic encephalomalacia surrounded by gliosis
suggesting a remote focal brain injury

concepts.why: The patient's brain MRI shows significant atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere, areas of cystic encephalomalacia, and evidence suggesting a remote focal brain injury, which are consistent with a hemispheric stroke.
The patient's seizures began at age 3 months, and the brain MRI shows evidence of a remote focal brain injury, which could be consistent with a perinatal stroke.
The patient has left-sided weakness, developmental delays, significant cognitive impairment, and marked left hemiparesis, which are consistent with cerebral palsy.
The patient has recurrent seizures, focal abnormal brain activity on EEG, and evidence of a remote focal brain injury on MRI, which could be consistent with Rasmussen's encephalitis.
The patient has seizures, left-sided weakness, significant cognitive impairment, and evidence of a remote focal brain injury on MRI, which could be consistent with Sturge-Weber syndrome.
